conviction_note: Each finding is small and they roughly cancel. The fundamental read is a modest beat: strong Q3 spending at JPM, Citi, BofA and Delta, Q3 write-offs below Q2 in AXP's own 8-K, and card-fee acceleration the company already guided. Against that, the reaction function: AXP fell after 6 of its last 7 prints, including -4.3% on a Q2 beat with a raised revenue guide, and it has run +6.8% off its early-October low into this print. Q3 GAAP EPS also carries two one-offs: a ~$975M pre-tax GBTG gain (closed 2026-09-29, outside the FY guide) and the unreserved part of a $350M OCC penalty. These make the headline EPS a poor signal. abs_move is held at 4.0, near the 4.49 implied move and above the 3.15 mean of the history, and p_up sits at 51. The findings sum (-0.10) and the scaled number (+0.08) are both effectively zero, so they do not really disagree.

The sources agree. EPS sources are spread: $4.47 (Zacks, two downward revisions in 7 days), $4.54 (Fiscal AI), $4.58 (Earnings Whispers), $4.59-4.60 (Benzinga). All exclude the ~$1.10/share GBTG gain. The company guide is FY2026 revenue growth of 10% and EPS of $17.30-17.90, explicitly ex-gain (https://sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/4962/000000496226000318/q226exhibit991.htm). The revenue bar is consistent with the guide: H2 needs ~+9.3% and consensus Q3 is +9.2% on $18.43B.
positioning_check: Short interest is about 11.5M shares, ~1.7% of ~675M shares outstanding, at 3.8 days to cover. This is the FINRA 2026-07-15 settlement via a curvedtrading.com search snippet (snippet_only; the page returned 403; https://curvedtrading.com/stocks/axp/short-interest/). It was 10.8M / 2.9 days at 2026-06-30. Not a crowded short. The baseline skew is +0.65 vol points (balanced), put/call OI 1.25, and front-expiry OI is thin (5,197). The event-implied move of 4.49% is rich against a 2.35% median historical reaction. The stock is -15.9% from its 52-week high and up +5.91% over 20 days. It traded near $303 pre-market on 2026-10-05 (stocktwits) and $323.71 at the seal, after Barclays, UBS and Evercore cut targets to $342/$345/$320.

findings.finding: AXP's own 8-K of 2026-10-15 shows Q3 2026 U.S. Consumer card net write-offs (principal only) at 1.6%, against 1.8% in Q2 2026. Q2 had been flattered ~0.3pp in June by a sale of written-off balances, so the underlying improvement is ~0.3pp. U.S. Small Business was 2.3% against 2.4%. Held-for-investment balances grew to $160.9B from $159.7B. 30+ day delinquency ticked up to 1.2% (Consumer) from 1.1%, and to 1.4% (Small Business) from 1.3/1.4%. Q3 2025 company-wide net write-offs were 1.9% and Q3 2025 provision was $1,287M (Q2 2026 deck). Lower write-offs point to a provision at or below Q2's $1,084M against a large y/y comparison, which supports EPS ex-items above the $4.47-4.60 consensus. The delinquency uptick limits any reserve release.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: In Q2 2026, credit was strong (a $191M reserve release, write-offs flat at 2.0%) and EPS beat ($4.53 vs ~$4.41), yet the stock fell 4.3% on the print day (baseline 2026-07-24) because the EPS guide was held. Credit beats have not been paid for on this name.
findings.why_not_priced: It is public eight days before the print and sell-side models read it, so it is largely in consensus. Zacks nonetheless shows two downward EPS revisions in the last seven days, not upward ones. If the market had fully priced lower write-offs, revisions would be drifting up rather than down.
findings.independence: JPMorgan Q3 2026 Card Services NCO fell to 2.91% from 3.15% y/y (https://www.pymnts.com/?p=4306652). Citi U.S. cards NCLs were down 4% y/y (https://www.panabee.com/news/citigroup-earnings-q3-2026). These are different issuers, so they point the same way independently.

findings.finding: Delta's September-quarter 2026 release (2026-10-09) is a direct counterparty that spoke after AXP last did. It reports American Express remuneration +15% y/y (Q2: +16%, $2.4B), co-brand card acquisitions and spend both growing double digits for the eighth straight quarter, and FY remuneration above $9B. Delta's corporate sales grew double digits in all sectors and its total revenue rose ~16% on yields. This supports AXP's T&E billed business (T&E is 28% of billed business, airlines 6%; Q2 T&E +10%) and card-fee growth, at about the Q2 pace with no acceleration.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Billed-business growth of 9% with a raised revenue guide in Q2 2026 still drew a -4.3% day. Billing strength on its own has not moved this stock up.
findings.why_not_priced: Public and read by card analysts. The remuneration growth rate is steady, not accelerating (15% vs 16%), so it confirms the run-rate in consensus rather than exceeding it. Had the market treated it as upside, revenue estimates would sit above the $20.27B that a straight 10% y/y implies, and they sit at $20.13B.
findings.independence: Delta's Q2 2026 release (https://s2.q4cdn.com/181345880/files/doc_earnings/2026/q2/earnings-result/Delta-Air-Lines-Announces-Second-Quarter-2026.pdf) gives the comparison. The industry spend finding below comes from different documents.

findings.finding: Q3 2026 card spending was strong at other issuers that reported after AXP's last print. JPMorgan debit and credit sales volume was +10% y/y to ~$539.5B. Citi general-purpose credit card spend was +13% y/y, flattered by the American Airlines portfolio onboarding. BofA Institute's September card spending per household was +6.2% y/y, the 'third strongest in four years', with breadth across income cohorts. Against AXP's own Q2 billed-business growth of +9% FX-adjusted, this is consistent with billed business holding ~9% or better and revenue at or slightly above the 9.2% y/y in consensus. It is a proxy only: AXP's affluent and commercial mix differs, and Commercial Services grew only 5% in Q2.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 revenue was $19.64B against ~$19.70B consensus, a slight miss despite +9% billings, and the stock fell. Revenue lines have decided the reaction here more than EPS.
findings.why_not_priced: These are wire-level macro prints, so the market has seen them. The transmission to AXP's own billings is unconfirmed. If it were fully priced, the revenue consensus would already have moved above the 10% FY guide pace, and it has not.
findings.independence: BofA Institute Consumer Checkpoint, 2026-10-09 (https://institute.bankofamerica.com/economic-insights/consumer-checkpoint-october-2026.html). Citi Q3 2026 (https://vestedfinance.com/blog/us-stocks/citigroup-q3-earnings-2026/). These are separate documents from JPM's. The Delta finding is a separate counterparty.

findings.finding: The GBTG stake sale closed inside Q3: Long Lake completed the GBTG take-private on 2026-09-29. AXP had said it would book ~$975M pre-tax gain on ~$1.5B proceeds, 'not factored into the FY 2026 earnings guidance', and would 'invest a portion... and return a portion to shareholders'. At a ~24% tax rate that is ~$740M, or roughly +$1.10 on Q3 GAAP EPS against a $4.47-4.60 consensus that excludes it. The headline EPS will read as a large beat, and the FY GAAP guide may be lifted to include the gain. The market will look through it. It matters only through how much is redeployed into marketing and buybacks, and whether the ex-gain EPS guide moves.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No same-line history in the baseline. In Q2 2026 the 'reaffirm EPS guide with increased investments' framing drew -4.3%, so redeploying gains into spend has not been rewarded.
findings.why_not_priced: The gain itself is public, and a below-the-line gain is seen through, so its price value is near zero. What is not priced is the use of the gain. If the market expected it to fund a buyback or a guide raise, the stock would not be trading 16% below its high with target cuts into the print.
findings.independence: The closing date comes from GBTG's 8-K exhibit (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001820872/000114036126037931/ef20082602_ex99-1.htm) and AXP's Q2 10-Q ('sizable pre-tax gain... in Other expense', https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/4962/000000496226000322/axp-20260630.htm). It shares the 'invest a portion' language with the expense finding, which is sized net of this.

findings.finding: On 2026-10-08 AENB consented to an OCC cease-and-desist order with a $350M civil money penalty, plus a Fed order, over BSA/AML deficiencies (~$13B of suspected trade-based laundering went unreported). AXP says a portion was reserved in prior periods; the Q2 10-Q cites 'an increase in legal reserves'. There is no asset cap, and AXP says there is no impact on FY2026 or 2027 guidance. The unreserved remainder, which is non-deductible, will likely be booked as a Q3 charge because the order came before the books closed. Its size is undisclosed: it could be roughly $0.05-0.25 per share.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: None in the baseline. The news itself landed 2026-10-08, during the +6.8% rebound from early-October lows, so the market did not treat it as material.
findings.why_not_priced: The headline is priced. The Q3 charge remainder is not quantified anywhere, and it may be part of why Zacks consensus drifted down to $4.47. It is a one-off with no stated path to the guide, so it is sized near zero.
findings.independence: OCC release (https://occ.gov/news-issuances/news-releases/2026/nr-occ-2026-87.html). Banking Dive (https://www.bankingdive.com/news/amex-dinged-by-fed-occ-must-pay-350m-for-aml-failures/832570/): no reserved figure given.

findings.finding: Expense pressure, from AXP's Q2 2026 deck. Total expenses grew +12% against revenue +10%. Card Member Services was +50% ($1,949M vs $1,301M) on the U.S. Platinum refresh and benefit usage. Variable customer engagement costs were 44.6% of revenue (+17%). The EPS guide was held 'with increased investments in growth opportunities'. With the GBTG gain earmarked partly for investment, Q3 marketing and opex are likely to step up. That risks a weaker pre-tax margin ex-gain and a 'quality of beat' read even if revenue lands.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026: EPS beat, expenses +12%, guide held, -4.3% on the day (baseline). The market has punished expense growth outrunning revenue growth.
findings.why_not_priced: The run-rate is known. What is unknown is the size of Q3 redeployment funded by the gain. If the market expected spend to be contained, there would be no valuation-led target cuts (Evercore to $320, UBS to $345) into the print.
findings.independence: This shares the GBTG 'invest a portion' release with the one-off finding; that finding is sized net of this redeployment. Q2 10-Q expense commentary: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/4962/000000496226000322/axp-20260630.htm

findings.finding: AXP guided at Q2 that net card fee growth (15% FX-adjusted in Q2) would accelerate in Q3 and exit Q4 in the high teens, helped by the Platinum refresh, now 'the fastest growing' U.S. Consumer portfolio. Public Platinum welcome offers in October 2026 run up to 175,000 MR points on the $895 card, with higher offers tested in August, which is consistent with an acquisition push. This lands inside what the company already guided.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Card fees grew 15-17% through 2025-26 while the stock fell after most prints. This line has not driven reactions.
findings.why_not_priced: It is guided, so consensus carries it. Only a miss on the acceleration would surprise, and nothing found suggests one.
findings.independence: Motley Fool October 2026 offer roundup (https://www.fool.com/money/credit-cards/articles/best-amex-cards-this-month-oct-2026/). This is a proxy for acquisition intensity, not fee revenue.

findings.finding: Positioning and reaction function. AXP fell after 6 of its last 7 prints (median |move| 2.35%; -4.3% on 2026-07-24 after an EPS beat with a raised revenue guide and a held EPS guide; -4.31% on 2026-04-23). It now enters the print up ~6.8% from its ~$303 early-October low to $323.71 (5-day +3.14%). In early October, Barclays ($342), UBS ($345) and Evercore ($320) cut targets on sector valuation (inflation, AI concerns), and the Koyfin split is 14 Hold vs 15 Buy. Short interest is not crowded (~1.7%), so there is no squeeze mechanism. A sell-the-news reaction to an ordinary beat is the base case for this name.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Baseline: 1 up in 7 (+7.27% on 2025-10-17, the only up print, which came with a guide raise). Every print without an EPS-guide raise has fallen.
findings.why_not_priced: The options are balanced (skew +0.65) and the implied move of 4.49% is nearly double the median reaction, so the market prices size, not sign. The rebound into the print raises the bar for 'good enough'. If the market had priced a sell-the-news outcome, the stock would not have rallied ~7% in the last two and a half weeks.
findings.independence: Sealed baseline reaction history (8-K 2.02 acceptance times). Q2 reaction coverage: https://www.hl.co.uk/shares/stock-market-news/company--news/american-express-lifts-revenue-outlook-after-strong-quarter,-but-shares-fall

outside_window.finding: OCC order requires an action plan within 90 days and a third-party SAR look-back; any further remediation cost or business restriction surfaces after the window.
Visa and Mastercard September-quarter prints (cross-border and U.S. payments volume read-through) are scheduled after 2026-10-23, so the market cannot see them inside the window.

baseline_tension: The fundamentals lean mildly positive, but the history (6 of 7 prints down), the +6.8% rebound into the print and valuation-led target cuts lean against them; the balanced skew (+0.65) and a rich 4.49% implied move say the market prices size, not direction, which is where this lands too.
lessons_applied: Rule 1 (a verified fact is not a predicted reaction; this name sells its beats): the reported-quarter credit, Delta and industry-spend findings were each cut from +0.3 to +0.2, and p_up moved from 52 to 51.
Rule 2 (one-offs sized as one-offs): the GBTG gain went from +0.2 to +0.1 and the OCC penalty from -0.15 to -0.05; neither has a stated path to the ex-gain guide.
Rule 6 (inside the guide): card-fee acceleration was already guided by the company, so it went from +0.1 to +0.05.

Rules 3 and 5: the expense finding and the GBTG finding share the 'invest a portion' language. Both are kept, with the GBTG finding sized net of redeployment. The industry spend finding is labelled a proxy. No finding was dropped.
Rule 7: short interest was checked before the negative positioning finding (~1.7%, 3.8 days, not crowded), so the -0.6 was left as it was.
